correctness.rationale: PASS. The least integer with h(m)≥k is E_k (E_1=2, E_{k+1}=2^{E_k}) by induction on the largest prime-power exponent. For factorials ν_p(N!)≤ν₂(N!); Legendre gives ν₂((E_{k−1}+1)!)=E_{k−1}−1 and ν₂((E_{k−1}+2)!)=E_{k−1} for k≥3, hence first hits F_k=E_{k−1}+2, F_1=2,F_2=4. For initial LCM, ν_p L(N)=floor(log_p N) gives first hits G_k=E_k and entire [E_k,2E_k) constant plateau. At 2E_k the 2-adic exponent is E_{k−1}+1, whose recursive height is too small; all odd-prime exponents <E_{k−1}. Exact lower bound at drop follows from prime p with ν_p L(2E_k)=a=E_{k−2}, by explicit p=5 for k3 and p=11 for k4, and Bertrand in (N^(1/(a+1)),N^(1/a)) for k≥5. The proof handles all k without enumerating impossible huge tower indices. Independently calculated factorial and LCM heights at all reachable first-hit and double endpoints through k4, and factorial k5=65538; computations corroborate, not replace the induction.
